counterfactual_missing_items: no classic progressive nodular centripetal fill is described
no central scar is described to support FNH
no intralesional fat, hemorrhage, or steroid/contraceptive risk context is described to support hepatocellular adenoma
decisive_items: hypointense mass on T1-weighted images containing several hyperintense areas on T2-weighted images
On diffusion-weighted imaging (b = 1000), the lesion was hyperintense relative to liver, with ADC values of 2.11×10^−3 mm^2/s peripherally and 2.45×10^−3 mm^2/s centrally (mean 2.33×10^−3 mm^2/s)
the lesion remained hypointense in the hepatobiliary phase
response.rationale: R2 best reconciles T2-hyperintense foci, very high ADC, absent FDG uptake, and hepatobiliary-phase hypointensity; the HBP pattern specifically disfavors FNH, which should retain hepatobiliary contrast. R1 shares nonspecific mass/enzyme findings but lacks a defining adenoma feature such as fat, hemorrhage, or anabolic/contraceptive context. Atypical ring enhancement and lack of pooling lower confidence, hence medium margin.

rejected.why: Hepatobiliary-phase hypointensity and absence of a central scar are inconsistent with typical FNH, which characteristically appears iso/hyperintense in the hepatobiliary phase.
